req.title: Create schema on startup
req.statement: The system shall create the tasks table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-024 requires that the tasks table is created via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup. The primary observable effect is that the app is reachable (HTTP 2xx on root) and that CRUD endpoints work against the created schema immediately after import — proving the table exists. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — root endpoint returns 200 with exact payload after startup; (2) positive EP — GET /tasks/ returns HTTP 200 and a list (schema exists and is queryable); (3) negative NEG — POST /tasks/ with missing required field returns 422 (client error, schema is live and validates); (4) boundary BVA — GET /tasks/ with skip=0 and limit=1 returns exactly one row, confirming the table was populated and the boundary constant is correct; (5) STC — app import triggers create_all, then immediate POST+GET round-trip proves the table is writable from the first request.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_root_returns_200_exact_payload():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["message"] == "Welcome to Task Manager API"
    assert body["docs"] == "/docs"
    assert body["version"] == "1.0.0"
    assert len(body) == 3

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_tasks_table_exists_and_queryable():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    if len(body) > 0:
        item = body[0]
        assert "id" in item
        assert "title" in item
        assert "completed" in item
        assert "created_at" in item
        assert isinstance(item["id"], int)
        assert isinstance(item["completed"], bool)

test_startup_tasks_table_exists_and_queryable()

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_tasks_limit_boundary_one():

    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    assert len(body) == 1
    item = body[0]
    assert item["id"] == 1
    assert item["title"] == "Read chapter 5"

tests.name: test_startup_create_and_retrieve_task_round_trip
preconditions: App imported; create_all executed at module load
tasks table writable from first request
expected: Response body has id, title matching input, completed=false
GET returns HTTP 200 with same id and title
trace: R-TASK-024 — STC: startup -> writable table -> create -> retrieve; proves schema fully operational from first request
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_create_and_retrieve_task_round_trip():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Startup test task", "description": "created in test", "completed": False}
    r_post = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    created = r_post.json()
    assert created["title"] == "Startup test task"
    assert created["completed"] == False
    assert isinstance(created["id"], int)
    task_id = created["id"]
    r_get = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    fetched = r_get.json()
    assert fetched["id"] == task_id
    assert fetched["title"] == "Startup test task"
    assert fetched["completed"] == False

test_startup_create_and_retrieve_task_round_trip()
